entities.name: Query UbiE methyltransferase
observations: 262 aa sequence; predicted molecular weight 28,936 Da and theoretical pI 5.97.
Strong homology support for UbiE, with 70.9–72.0% identity and 93.9–94.3% query coverage to reviewed bacterial UbiE proteins.
Best-supported role is a ubiquinone/menaquinone biosynthesis C-methyltransferase using S-adenosyl-L-methionine.
Exact substrate usage can vary between UbiE homologs; sequence evidence supports family-level activity more strongly than one exclusive substrate.

entities.name: UbiE quinone C-methylation
observations: Demethylmenaquinol + S-adenosyl-L-methionine -> menaquinol + S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + H+; mapped to Rhea 42640.
2-methoxy-6-(all-trans-polyprenyl)benzene-1,4-diol + S-adenosyl-L-methionine -> 5-methoxy-2-methyl-3-(all-trans-polyprenyl)benzene-1,4-diol + S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + H+; mapped to Rhea 28286.
The transformation is transfer of a methyl group from SAM to a quinone/quinol ring, producing SAH.

entities.name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine
observations: Methyl donor for the UbiE-catalyzed quinone-ring methylation reaction.

entities.name: Menaquinone biosynthesis
observations: UbiE is annotated in the menaquinone biosynthetic process and quinol/quinone metabolism.
The enzyme catalyzes the terminal methylation step in the menaquinol branch from 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate, according to reviewed homolog annotations.
